narrative.text:
I’ll verify the upstream baseline, trace event tagging and account identity, then add tests and run the requested base/head gates on both Node versions. I won’t push anything.Upstream already suppresses own live and history messages when the startup profile lookup returns a user ID. That lookup is awaited, but it isn’t retried: if it fails, own messages can reach the host, and reconnecting doesn’t repair the identity. Changes made by others to the bot’s messages also intentionally reach the host.

I’ll preserve that suppression, tag the remaining own-message events using ID-first/email-fallback matching, and leave reactions governed by who reacted—not who authored the target message.The new tests are passing, including a real `zulip-js` HTTP-path test that reproduces own-message delivery after a failed profile lookup. I’ve also checked that ID-based suppression remains intact, tags survive backscroll and recovery, and mixed-author catch-up blocks are not marked as self.

I’m committing the change, then running the full head gates on both requested Node versions.
